vision: One paragraph: who the product is for, what it must be trusted for, and the order of work (R1 makes it trustworthy, R2 adds depth, R3 adds what competitors lack).

releases.name: R1 Foundation and integrity
releases.goal: Close the integrity defects and make parallel work possible: split the monolith first (one serial track), then give every later track its own files.

tracks.summary: Runs alone first. Characterisation test of the route table, then a mechanical move of every route into src/server/routes/<domain>.ts. Adds the transaction, audit and validation primitives and the test harness.
Forward-only, versioned migrations with a verified backup before any upgrade of an installed database.
One signing service: password re-entered, meaning from a catalogue, bound to the record version, audit entry in the same transaction.
Hash-chained, append-only audit trail with on-demand verification and a reason for change.

releases.name: R2 Feature depth
releases.goal: Features buyers expect. Core tables are frozen (their columns feed signed hashes): a feature adds a sidecar table and its own route, guard and schedule files in the registries.

tracks.summary: Controlled certificate: gap-free number, e-signature, stored PDF with its SHA-256.

gaps.title: Platform core: split the monolith, transactional primitives, test harness
gaps.currentStateEvidence: src/server/api.ts holds 64 routes in one router (wc -l: 3012). No test framework: grep -r vitest package.json -> nothing.
gaps.design: Route modules per domain, createRouter/asyncHandler, withTransaction, updateVersioned, writeAudit; Vitest with a real database per test file.
acceptance: tests/route-table.json lists the same routes before and after the move.
A write with a stale version answers 409 and changes nothing.
gaps.gxpRisk: Every later control (audit, signature, concurrency) depends on these primitives being the only write path.

gaps.title: Versioned migrations for installed databases
gaps.competitorBenchmark: Incumbents ship upgrade scripts with a backup step.
gaps.currentStateEvidence: Schema is pushed with drizzle-kit push; no migrations folder (ls migrations -> no such directory).
gaps.design: Numbered SQL migrations, a schema_migrations table, a runner that refuses a database it does not recognise, backup before upgrade.
acceptance: A v0.1.0 database upgrades with every earlier signature still verifying.
A database ahead of the code is refused with a readable message.
gaps.gxpRisk: An upgrade that rewrites signed columns invalidates signatures.

gaps.title: Electronic signature service
gaps.competitorBenchmark: Signature manifestation with meaning, bound to the record.
gaps.currentStateEvidence: Three components verify the password in the browser (src/components/Sign.tsx:41).
gaps.design: signRecord(tx, { entity, id, version, meaning, password, totp }).
acceptance: A wrong password creates no signature and is audited.
A signature made against version 3 does not verify against version 4.
gaps.gxpRisk: Part 11 signature binding; do not cite clauses you have not read.

gaps.title: Audit trail v2
gaps.competitorBenchmark: Field-level history with reason for change and review.
gaps.currentStateEvidence: audit rows carry no reason; UPDATE on audit_trail is possible for the application role.
gaps.design: Append-only triggers, hash chain, reason for change past draft.
acceptance: UPDATE and DELETE on audit_trail fail for every role.
One changed byte fails verification and names the row.
gaps.gxpRisk: The audit trail is the record of record changes.

gaps.title: Controlled certificate
gaps.competitorBenchmark: CoA with version control and re-issue.
gaps.currentStateEvidence: Reports.tsx prints 'ALL TESTS PASSED' regardless of results (line 236).
gaps.design: Issue only for an approved record; supersede with reason.
acceptance: A record with a failing result cannot get a certificate stating compliance.
gaps.gxpRisk: A certificate is a released GxP statement.
